Glaucoma

The only patient trial was retracted because of potentially significant errors in irradiation parameters and dose calculations. The remaining evidence is a review and a laboratory cell study.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

The only patient trial was retracted because of potentially significant errors in irradiation parameters and dose calculations. The remaining evidence is a review and a laboratory cell study.

Summary of the Evidence

Three publications appear in the exact glaucoma category: one review, one human pilot trial that was formally retracted, and one in-vitro trabecular-meshwork experiment. The retracted report should not be treated as valid efficacy evidence. The journal cited potentially significant errors in clinically relevant irradiation parameters and dose calculations; the authors disputed the retraction. Journal retraction notice,: PubMed.

Human and clinical evidence

The 2015 pilot described 38 patients and 63 eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma and reported visual and intraocular-pressure changes. The journal later retracted the article after identifying possible errors in treatment dose and calculation that could create risk if used clinically. Because of that retraction, its numerical efficacy claims are not relied upon here. No unretracted randomized or observational clinical trial demonstrating benefit was identified in the mapped category.

Animal evidence

No animal study directly treating glaucoma was identified in the exact category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One cell-monolayer experiment studied low-fluence diode irradiation and hydraulic conductivity in cultured trabecular meshwork endothelial cells. It reports different responses in viable and nonviable monolayers. This laboratory result does not measure intraocular pressure, optic-nerve progression, or vision in patients.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The retracted trial used a photobiomodulation protocol whose irradiation and dose calculations were questioned by the journal. The cell experiment used a different low-fluence diode setup. These protocols are not interchangeable, and a safe, reproducible clinical dose cannot be inferred from the remaining evidence.

Interpretation

There is no reliable clinical evidence in this mapped set that PBM improves glaucoma outcomes. The retracted trial cannot support a treatment recommendation, and cell-level responses do not establish patient benefit. Any further clinical evaluation would need independently verified dosimetry, safety monitoring, and validated glaucoma endpoints.

Publications and records3 publications: 1 review, 1 human pilot trial, and 1 in-vitro experiment.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The only identified patient trial was formally retracted after the journal cited potentially important problems in irradiation parameters and dose calculations. A review and one cell experiment remain, but they do not establish clinical benefit, sustained pressure control, or safety in patients.

Publication and study types

  • The only clinical report is retracted and is excluded from efficacy conclusions.
  • It enrolled 38 patients and 63 eyes, but no usable independent clinical cohort remains.
  • No animal study or unretracted clinical outcome study is listed.
